$comment: The `__SIZEOF_*__` family PREDEFINED, each equal to `sizeof` of the type it names (D-C-SIZEOF-PREDEFINED-MACRO-FAMILY-MISSING): SHORT, INT, LONG, LONG_LONG, FLOAT, DOUBLE, LONG_DOUBLE, POINTER, SIZE_T, PTRDIFF_T, WCHAR_T (through the `<stddef.h>` typedef AND `L'a'`), WINT_T (no narrower than WCHAR_T) and INT128. The file stops at an `#error` when a member is undefined and at a `_Static_assert` when one disagrees with its type; at run time a pointer must survive a copy of exactly `__SIZEOF_POINTER__` bytes (11), arrays must stride by the stated sizes (12, 14), and all-ones `long`/`size_t` values must fill them (13, 15) — `main.c` lists the codes. The values are each PAIR's own: `long` 8 on Linux and Apple and 4 on Windows, `long double` 16/16/8/8 on x86_64 Linux / aarch64 Linux / Windows (binary64, the MSVC ABI) / Apple arm64 and 16 on Apple x86_64, `wchar_t`/`wint_t` 2 on Windows and 4 elsewhere. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-22, each reference separately: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 run it to 42 on x86_64 Linux and aarch64 Linux (qemu) at -O0 and -O2; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 runs it to 42 at -O0 and -O2 (its `long double` is x87 in 16 bytes, consistent with itself); clang compiles it clean (-c, -O0 and -O2) for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, arm64-apple-macos11 and x86_64-apple-macos11. MSVC predefines no `__SIZEOF_*` name (the GNU extension gcc and clang share). ✔MEASURED at the P68 round-8 part-4 base: DSS stopped at `#error "__SIZEOF_SHORT__ is not predefined"` on all five targets, debug and release. ★ The `release` arm: every run-time value comes from a `volatile`.
